papers.abstract_zh: 权重剪枝可以降低大语言模型（LLMs）的存储和推理成本，但在高稀疏度水平下保持质量仍然具有挑战性。现有方法在这一情形下面临质量与成本之间的权衡。一次性剪枝成本低廉，但随着稀疏度增加会急剧退化，即使随后进行剪枝后恢复也是如此。越来越多的工作转而以端到端目标直接从稠密模型优化掩码；在这些方法中，[Lee et al.,2026] 作为极端稀疏度下最新的 state of the art，达到了高质量，但代价是需要与模型规模相当的优化器状态和辅助变量。为弥补这一空白，我们提出 ETAPS，它逐步剪枝并稀疏适应：它在渐进阶段中收紧全局稀疏约束，同时以小的固定预算训练一个稀疏 delta。我们的关键观察是，逐步移除权重使每一步剪枝都足够小，从而可由稀疏适应来补偿，使适应后的模型能够提供端到端梯度来指导下一步剪枝决策，而无需与模型规模相当的优化器状态。在从 125M 到 13B 参数的六个模型上，ETAPS 在 50% 到 90% 的每一个评估稀疏度下都取得了比 ELSA 更低的困惑度，困惑度降低最高达 42%。ETAPS 也便宜得多：在 90% 稀疏度下，它可在单块 H200 上剪枝 LLaMA2-7B，而 ELSA 使用四块，总持久状态小 $5.0\times$，GPU 小时数减少 49%。总之，我们的发现指向了一个有前景的方向：以显著更低的成本在诸如极端稀疏度这样的严苛情形下实现高质量。

papers.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
papers.summary: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control. Such gains are credible only when candidates carry exploitable signal, nominal compute savings become real speedup, and evaluation stays reliable. We audit all three on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa with a premise-first, pre-registered methodology. On clean data, a learned value selector is 1.66 pp worse than random; a hindsight oracle gains only 1.40 pp, with an episode-level interval spanning zero; and 82% of states show identical candidate outcomes, leaving little selection headroom. Token pruning cuts per-forward FLOPs by up to 47% but yields at most a measured 1.15$\times$ end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.25$\times$ on a decode-excluded path), short of a 1.5$\times$ target, and our adaptive-allocation experiment is inconclusive under a power gate. We further identify and fix a silent rendering corruption whose rate rises sharply along compute-heavy planning paths while leaving the official direct-policy result unaffected, and release a detector, fix, and scripts. These findings show why test-time scaling should be audited as a chain of premises (decision signal, realized efficiency, evaluationintegrity) rather than by success rate alone. Conclusions are scoped to the tested configuration.

papers.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
papers.summary: Large-scale behavioral pretraining offers a promising route to generalizable representations in online payment systems. However, high-cardinality identity fields such as card, device, and account IDs, though rich in behavioral signals, remain underexploited. Their continually growing vocabularies and limited semantic meaning make existing vocabulary-based and semantics-based encodings ill-suited. Their generalizable signal lies not in specific values, but in the identity behavior patterns they exhibit across a transaction sequence. Building on this insight, we propose ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that brings these patterns into transaction foundation models. ID2Pattern first encodes identity fields with a Local Anonymous ID (LAID) tokenizer, which captures how each identity appears and recurs within the sequence, independent of its specific value. It then pretrains a multi-scale pattern codebook on unlabeled sequences, which abstracts LAID sequences into discrete behavior patterns for downstream prediction. Experiments on an industrial dataset with over 100M sequences and six public datasets show that ID2Pattern consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving industrial by 4.13% and public datasets by 8.83% on average. Notably, ID2Pattern remains equally effective even when all identity values are unseen during training, highlighting its potential to generalize to new users and markets.

papers.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
papers.summary: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. Therefore, we introduce Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures these parameters before training. DAMI assigns geometric timescales across heads for varied retrieval distances and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers. A small activation sample calibrates the GDN-family implementation to match both behavioral targets without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI improves average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over the corresponding random-initialization baselines. Performance on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remains broadly comparable to those baselines. Our code is available at https://speedai.com/research/dami.

papers.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
papers.summary: Multi-turn negotiation remains a challenging problem for large language model (LLM) agents. While LLMs can conduct natural-language dialogue, existing benchmarks predominantly assess only agreement rates, overlooking whether negotiated commitments actually create value once executed. To address this gap, we introduce TradeWar, a multi-country simulation benchmark that translates negotiation dialogues into concrete tariff and trade-share policies, enforces capacity and network constraints during settlement, and evaluates outcomes via an Economic Health Index (EHI). To solve this execution-grounded task, we propose TACTIC (Trade-aware Adaptive Consolidation and Theory-of-mind for International Commerce), an agent that iteratively refines its negotiation strategy across episodes-without updating base LLM weights-by leveraging prior experience, opponent behavior, and past settlement outcomes. Despite using zero-shot chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, PromptLLM attains a 75% agreement rate but only 57.1 final EHI (*100), whereas TACTIC reaches 68.8. Across 20 sequential episodes and three seeds, TACTIC's final EHI improves from 58.2 to 73.2, compared with 65.2 for an ablation without cross-episode updates. Under technology-controls and energy-crisis shocks, TACTIC also exhibits smaller performance degradation than PromptLLM and MemoryLLM. These results indicate that CoT deliberation and interaction memory alone do not fully address delayed execution feedback, whereas settlement-grounded adaptation improves long-horizon negotiation in TradeWar.
papers.title_zh: TradeWar：一个面向执行落地的自适应LLM智能体贸易谈判基准
papers.abstract_zh: 多轮谈判仍然是大型语言模型（LLM）智能体面临的一个具有挑战性的问题。尽管LLM能够进行自然语言对话，但现有基准主要仅评估协议达成率，忽视了谈判承诺在执行后是否真正创造价值。为弥补这一空白，我们提出TradeWar，一个多国模拟基准，它将谈判对话转化为具体的关税与贸易份额政策，在结算过程中强制执行产能与网络约束，并通过经济健康指数（EHI）评估结果。为解决这一以执行为基础的任务，我们提出TACTIC（Trade-aware Adaptive Consolidation and Theory-of-mind for International Commerce），一种无需更新基础LLM权重、通过利用先前经验、对手行为和过往结算结果在多个回合间迭代优化其谈判策略的智能体。尽管使用零样本思维链（CoT）提示，PromptLLM达到75%的协议达成率，但最终EHI仅为57.1（*100），而TACTIC达到68.8。在20个连续回合和三个随机种子下，TACTIC的最终EHI从58.2提升到73.2，而无跨回合更新的消融版本为65.2。在技术管制和能源危机冲击下，TACTIC的性能退化也小于PromptLLM和MemoryLLM。这些结果表明，仅靠CoT推理和交互记忆并不能完全应对延迟的执行反馈，而基于结算的适应能够改善TradeWar中的长时程谈判。

papers.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
papers.summary: Hundreds of millions of people now ask large language model (LLM) chatbots for health advice, which raises a question that is simple to pose and hard to answer: does everyone get the same advice? We audit six widely deployed LLMs from four providers on smoking cessation, a domain with codified clini- cal guidance and substantial public-health stakes, by putting the same four cessation questions to twelve user personas that differ in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, for a total of 2,880 responses. What the models say depends on who appears to be asking. Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen personas than to adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points, and in five of six models a persona presenting health- care expertise received fewer facts than a persona presenting none. We then evaluate one deployable intervention: a short system prompt specifying a factual floor, the set of core med- ical facts every user should receive when they are relevant, while leaving tone, vocabulary, and framing free to adapt. The prompt narrows persona differences in every model, but its effect on overall fact coverage varies in both magnitude and direction across models, so a prompt validated on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another. Two cautions frame these results. Equal mention rates are not always the correct clinical target, because prescription cessation pharmacother- apy is not recommended for minors, so a defensible factual floor must be age-aware rather than uniform. And because our personas vary on several attributes at once, we report scenario- level differences rather than isolated effects of age or expertise. We release all 2,880 responses and the analysis code.
papers.title_zh: 同一个问题，不同的答案：审计六个LLM在戒烟建议中依赖用户画像的差异
papers.abstract_zh: 如今有数亿人向大型语言模型（LLM）聊天机器人寻求健康建议，这提出了一个容易提出却难以回答的问题：每个人得到的建议都一样吗？我们以戒烟为领域，审计来自四个提供方的六个广泛部署的LLM，该领域具有成文的临床指南和重大的公共卫生利害关系；我们向十二个在人生阶段、自述专业知识和吸烟史方面各不相同的用户画像提出同样的四个戒烟问题，共获得2,880条回答。模型所说的话取决于看起来是谁在提问。每个模型向青少年画像提及FDA批准的处方戒烟药物的频率都低于向成人画像提及的频率，低32至67个百分点；并且在六个模型中的五个里，表现出医疗保健专业知识的画像比未表现出任何专业知识的画像获得的事实更少。我们随后评估了一种可部署的干预措施：一个简短的系统提示，它规定一个事实底线，即当相关时每位用户都应获得的一组核心医学事实，同时让语气、词汇和框架自由调整。该提示缩小了每个模型中的画像差异，但其对总体事实覆盖的影响在不同模型之间无论在幅度还是方向上都存在差异，因此不能假定在一个系统上验证过的提示可以迁移到另一个系统。两点警示为这些结果划定了框架。相同的提及率并不总是正确的临床目标，因为处方戒烟药物治疗不推荐用于未成年人，所以一个站得住脚的事实底线必须考虑年龄，而不是统一不变。而且由于我们的画像同时在一个以上属性上发生变化，我们报告的是场景层面的差异，而不是年龄或专业知识的孤立效应。我们发布全部2,880条回答和分析代码。

papers.title: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results
papers.summary: AI answers require more than apparent correctness: reviewers need to inspect their recorded basis. We introduce the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), an open, implementation-neutral specification for inference records with versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit unknowns. SEDIM, the knowledge and evidence architecture of Nage AI OS, is a reference implementation. We reference KLM v0.3 (repository tag v0.3.0). Empirical material consists of separate internal experiments, not end-to-end validation. A historical platform-domain routing benchmark reports 137/150 classifications across 15 classes (91.3%; nominal 95% Wilson interval 85.7-94.9%); the numerator is recovered from a rounded summary, and historical example membership is unverified. A native-model weight-path configuration yielded 0/15 successful answers in a corrected two-source test. A capacity-growth comparison could not establish a reliable effect because of a defective legacy scorer and missing original outputs. Lexical and scoped diagnostics each yielded AUC 0.008 for silent-versus-contradicted examples, below the registered minimum of 0.65. Legacy packing lost gold-containing text in 118/221 selected cases; repaired packing retained it in 221/221. These measure text presence, not answer quality. Python and TypeScript verifiers reportedly agreed on six checks per synthetic fixture; a separate production disclosure was not accepted. Restoration, re-derivation, human-rubric support, boundary isolation, and bounded-response evaluations remain proposed. Findings are internal and author-reported; historical observations are distinguished from later reproductions. Evidence visibility does not establish correctness, causal reliance, security, or regulatory compliance. Independent replication and a complete public audit package remain future work.

papers.title: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models
papers.summary: World action models (WAMs) learn latent variables from observations and use these to both predict the evolution of the scene and to generate actions. The prediction has to be of the whole scene, whereas only a portion of the scene causes actions. WAMs fitted to demonstrations do not, in general, guarantee that they will generate actions solely from the latent causes of the demonstrated actions (the action-relevant latent variables), as the model could just as well learn to imitate in this way whilst entangling the action-relevant latent variables with the nuisance variables. We therefore separate out what causes action from what prediction depends on. We prove that under a sparsity constraint the latent variables used to generate actions are an invertible function of the action-relevant latent variables alone and the true structure is identified up to a permutation of the latent variables. This requires neither sufficient temporal dependence nor any assumptions on how the unobserved regimes evolve and holds even when the action-relevant latent variables are statistically dependent on the rest. We therefore propose CWAM (Causal WAM), which incorporates the constraint into a pretrained WAM by adding a sparse routing path to its action head, with the world modeling objective remaining unchanged. Experiments on both synthetic data and real-world robots validate the theory as well as showcase the improved efficiency in closed-loop success.

papers.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
papers.summary: In real-world deployments, large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly evolving from single-model invocation toward heterogeneous deployments in which different models are dynamically invoked for inference. When the same context is reused across models, however, each newly selected target model typically has to process it again, repeatedly incurring substantial computational costs. Therefore, we propose ACCT (Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer), which targets KV cache transfer between models of different scales within the same model family. ACCT transforms the KV cache produced by a source model into sparse KV states that can be directly consumed by a target model, thereby enabling cross-model reuse of context computation and decoupling context computation from downstream inference. ACCT consists of three lightweight components: the Cartographer identifies query-relevant context tokens for each target layer and KV head; the Allocator determines how many context tokens each target layer and KV head retains under a shared total KV budget; and the Compiler transforms selected source KV into sparse target KV. The target model can therefore perform inference using the transferred KV without reprocessing the original context. We evaluate ACCT in two complementary settings comprising five general-capability benchmarks and six highly context-dependent tasks. Experiments show that ACCT matches or exceeds the target model's original inference performance even when reducing the KV cache size by 75%. At a context length of approximately 19K tokens, ACCT's KV conversion achieves a 6.5-21.2 times speedup over target context prefill. These results demonstrate the feasibility of transferring context computation across models under a limited KV budget.
papers.title_zh: ACCT：非对称跨LLM上下文迁移
papers.abstract_zh: 在实际部署中，大型语言模型（LLM）系统正日益从单模型调用演进为异构部署，即动态调用不同模型进行推理。然而，当同一上下文在多个模型之间被复用时，每个新选定的目标模型通常都必须重新处理该上下文，从而反复产生大量计算开销。因此，我们提出ACCT（非对称跨LLM上下文迁移），其目标是在同一模型家族内不同规模的模型之间进行KV缓存迁移。ACCT将源模型产生的KV缓存转换为稀疏KV状态，这些状态可被目标模型直接使用，从而实现上下文计算的跨模型复用，并将上下文计算与下游推理解耦。ACCT由三个轻量级组件构成：Cartographer为每个目标层和KV头识别与查询相关的上下文token；Allocator在共享的总KV预算下确定每个目标层和KV头保留多少上下文token；Compiler将选定的源KV转换为稀疏的目标KV。因此，目标模型可以使用迁移而来的KV进行推理，而无需重新处理原始上下文。我们在两个互补的设置中评估ACCT，其中包括五个通用能力基准和六个高度依赖上下文的任务。实验表明，即使将KV缓存大小减少75%，ACCT仍能达到或超过目标模型原有的推理性能。在上下文长度约为19K token时，ACCT的KV转换相对于目标上下文预填充实现了6.5-21.2倍的加速。这些结果证明了在有限KV预算下跨模型迁移上下文计算的可行性。

papers.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
papers.summary: Agentic workflows are increasingly shifting towards long-horizon tasks, such as open-ended scientific work, where models benefit from long context windows. However, at ultra-long context (above 1M tokens), full attention is prohibitively expensive. A promising approach is sparse attention, in which a dedicated indexer selects a subset of keys for the attention. Yet current methods of indexing either still have quadratic cost in context size or lose accuracy at ultra-long context scale. We address this with Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), an efficient attention method that maintains accuracy at ultra-long context. In LSA, keys are hierarchically clustered in a learned latent space, and queries score the hierarchy of clusters instead of scoring every key, making prefill, decode and training faster at long context. We propose two variants, Distilled-LSA (D-LSA), which can be applied to pre-trained models via distillation, and Native-LSA (N-LSA), which is trained natively on the next-token loss alone. On GLM-5.3-FLASH (QWEN-3.8-27B) at 10M tokens, D-LSA speeds up one attention layer by 22.7x (72.4x) in prefill and 4.6x (42.5x) in decode over its original sparse attention (full attention), while keeping similar accuracy across a variety of tasks. N-LSA matches the accuracy of full attention with a training speedup of 1.6x per layer at 128k tokens. LSA offers practical and efficient attention for models to benefit from ultra-long context.

papers.title: HippocamFLEX: FPGA Prototyping of Hippocampus-Inspired Architecture for Context-Aware Sequence Prediction
papers.summary: Unlike conventional architectures that treat memory as static pattern storage, the hippocampus organizes experience as ordered sequences and retrieves them through temporally compressed replay spanning prior, current, and anticipated states. This capacity of context-appropriate sequence prediction remains absent from conventional deep learning accelerators and existing neuromorphic fabrics. We present HippocamFLEX, a fully synthesizable digital implementation of these hippocampal computational principles, realized with SystemVerilog RTL on the AMD Zynq UltraScale+,XCZU9EG. The design maps the hippocampal trisynaptic pathway onto three pipeline stages: a Dentate Gyrus / Entorhinal Cortex (DG/EC) stage for hypervector proximity matching, a CA3 stage for context-gated recurrent sequence prediction with multi-phase temporal tagging, and a CA1 stage that integrates past, present, and predicted future events into a theta-sequence inspired output. While much brain-inspired hardware relies on analog mixed-signal design for energy efficiency, this work targets FPGA prototyping as a deliberate architectural choice: FPGAs offer rapid design-space exploration without tape-out cost, bit-exact determinism that simplifies verification. The design supports 64 events across 16 contexts and is verified on physical silicon across context-isolation, temporal-ordering, and mid-sequence sliding-window test cases and is inherently scalable to larger event and context sets.

papers.title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
papers.summary: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses. Beyond characterization, nonlocality in multiscale systems is increasingly viewed as a design element across fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems. Existing nonlocality theories provide rigorous descriptions and mechanistic insight, but often require prescribed analytic forms, range, symmetries, or periodicity. Machine learning offers a data-driven route to learn interactions, yet principled approaches that tie the network design to physical theory remain nascent. Here we present domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations from field data alone. Through a case study in large-scale optical metasurfaces, we demonstrate DANO's full-field prediction under geometric heterogeneity and across drive conditions, small-to-large domain transfer, and multifunctional inverse design, with learned interactions validated through physics-based interrogation. As an AI-for-Science tool, it supports interaction discovery and scalable, customizable design of nonlocal multiscale systems, including virtual-reality optics.

papers.title: The Generative Gap Between Speculative Drafter and Continuous Diffusion Language Model
papers.summary: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) and speculative drafters offer efficient language generation but are typically evaluated differently: CDLMs generate independently through iterative refinement, whereas drafters propose text for target-model verification and correction. We compare their architectures without verification, using LangFlow for CDLMs and adapting DSpark's Markov and recurrent-head architectures for standalone generation. All models are trained from scratch for unconditional, single-block OpenWebText generation at lengths 16, 128, and 1024, without target features or verification, using common preprocessing, backbone dimensions, and training-update budgets. We evaluate generation perplexity (GenPPL) with an external language model and distributional similarity to reference text with MAUVE. With default denoising steps equal to sequence length, LangFlow outperforms both DSpark variants on both metrics at lengths 128 and 1024, while DSpark-RNN leads at 16. A conditional KL analysis characterizes dependencies excluded by the Markov head's previous-token conditioning. Recurrent memory removes this restriction and improves both metrics, but the longer-sequence gap persists. Teacher probability matching further lowers Markov GenPPL without observed MAUVE gains. Increasing LangFlow's denoising steps at fixed weights improves both metrics at lengths 16 and 128, changing the length-128 ordering relative to DSpark-RNN. These results establish LangFlow's longer-sequence advantage under the evaluated budgets and highlight iterative full-sequence refinement as a route to improving standalone generation beyond gains from recurrent head memory.
papers.title_zh: 投机草稿模型与连续扩散语言模型之间的生成差距
papers.abstract_zh: 连续扩散语言模型（CDLMs）与投机草稿器能够实现高效的语言生成，但通常以不同方式评估：CDLMs 通过迭代细化独立生成，而草稿器提出文本以供目标模型验证和修正。我们在不进行验证的情况下比较它们的架构，对 CDLMs 使用 LangFlow，并调整 DSpark 的马尔可夫架构和循环头架构以用于独立生成。所有模型均从头训练，用于无条件的单块 OpenWebText 生成，长度分别为 16、128 和 1024，不使用目标特征或验证，并采用共同预处理、骨干维度和训练更新预算。我们使用外部语言模型评估生成困惑度（GenPPL），并使用 MAUVE 评估与参考文本的分布相似性。在默认去噪步数等于序列长度时，LangFlow 在长度 128 和 1024 上在两个指标上均优于两个 DSpark 变体，而 DSpark-RNN 在 16 上领先。条件 KL 分析刻画了马尔可夫头的前一词元条件化所排除的依赖关系。循环记忆消除了这一限制并改善了两个指标，但较长序列上的差距仍然存在。教师概率匹配进一步降低了马尔可夫 GenPPL，但未观察到 MAUVE 增益。在固定权重下增加 LangFlow 的去噪步数可在长度 16 和 128 上改善两个指标，并改变长度 128 上相对于 DSpark-RNN 的排序。这些结果确立了在所评估预算下 LangFlow 的较长序列优势，并突出表明迭代式全序列细化是一条在循环头记忆带来的增益之外进一步改进独立生成的途径。

papers.title: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models
papers.summary: Fairness benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) are overwhelmingly English-born and American in their social categories; translated versions carry those categories into societies where they do not apply, and almost none fix their hypotheses before the models are run. We present Qistas (Arabic qistas, "the just balance"), a protocol for evaluating how LLMs treat the social, confessional, and regional constituencies of a society, portable across countries and instantiated first for Iraq. In its pilot form it measures only what needs no verdict on contested truth: procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, stereotype reliance under ambiguity, and terminological framing of documented events. Every measurement is paired by construction and analysed with paired machinery (sign-flip permutation tests, exact McNemar tests, template-clustered bootstrap intervals, Holm-corrected families), with a power analysis that states, before any data exist, the smallest effect each axis can detect after the design effect of template clustering. We release the authoring apparatus (a pruned 3x5 taxonomy with four cells closed by design, per-type checklists, a cumulative rulings log, a structural audit, and a human review notebook) and report its first field test: a semantic review of a 58-item seed bank in which 24 of 25 template groups failed at least one check. The defect patterns it exposed (evaluation criteria leaking into prompts, token-level swaps that break Arabic agreement, epistemically unbalanced pairs, single-theme refusal probes, unwritten dialect twins counted as coverage) are, we argue, general hazards of counterfactual fairness benchmarks. This is a protocol paper, not a results paper: no model has been evaluated, and the accompanying pre-registration commits the hypotheses, metrics, exclusion rules, and analysis plan that the pilot will follow.
papers.title_zh: Qistas：一个用于大型语言模型公平性评估的预注册、可移植协议
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）的公平性基准在语言上绝大多数源自英语，在社会类别上则是美国式的；翻译版本将这些类别带入它们并不适用的社会，而且几乎没有基准在模型运行之前预先确定其假设。我们提出 Qistas（阿拉伯语 qistas，意为“公正的天平”），这是一个用于评估 LLM 如何对待一个社会的社会、教派和地区构成群体的协议，可跨国家移植，并首先在伊拉克实例化。在其试点形式中，它只测量无需对有争议真相作出裁决的内容：匹配反事实对之间的程序对称性、差异性拒绝、歧义下的刻板印象依赖，以及对有记录事件的术语框定。每一项测量在构造上都是配对的，并使用配对方法进行分析（符号翻转置换检验、精确 McNemar 检验、模板聚类 bootstrap 区间、Holm 校正族），并附有一项功效分析，该分析在任何数据存在之前就说明每个轴在模板聚类的设计效应之后能够检测到的最小效应。我们发布编写装置（一个经剪枝的 3×5 分类法，其中四个单元按设计关闭；按类型检查清单；累积裁定日志；结构审计；以及人工审阅笔记本），并报告其首次现场测试：对一个 58 条目种子库的语义审查，其中 25 个模板组中有 24 个至少未通过一项检查。我们认为，它暴露出的缺陷模式（评估标准泄漏进提示词、破坏阿拉伯语一致性的词元级替换、认识论上不平衡的配对、单一主题的拒绝探测、将未写出的方言孪生项计为覆盖）是反事实公平性基准的普遍风险。这是一篇协议论文，而非结果论文：尚未评估任何模型，随附的预注册载明了试点将遵循的假设、指标、排除规则和分析计划。

papers.title: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Effective Multi-Turn Jailbreak
papers.summary: Automated red teaming trains an attacker large language model (LLM) to elicit harmful responses from a victim LLM, but reinforcement learning can collapse attackers onto a narrow set of prompts when attack success is the only reward. Such a collapse of attack diversity can bias safety evaluation toward repeatedly testing near-duplicate attack patterns rather than the underlying harmful intents. Existing methods often trade off attack success or inference cost for greater content or strategy diversity. We propose CoFiBreak, a coarse-to-fine diversity reward for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that improves attack diversity while preserving strong attack effectiveness and low inference cost. The coarse reward broadens which strategies the attacker uses by encouraging strategies underrepresented within each GRPO group, while the fine reward broadens how those strategies are realized by discouraging reuse of the same personas, framings, and output formats after harmful-intent information is removed from prompt embeddings. Diversity rewards apply only to attacks that already exceed an effectiveness threshold, so diversity cannot be gained through ineffective attacks. Since both rewards are computed only during training, CoFiBreak also retains inference efficiency. Trained with Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as the victim, CoFiBreak discovers 1.6-2.0x as many distinct successful fine-grained strategies as the strongest baseline across frontier victims on HarmBench. It reaches 98.8% ASR@10 (attack success rate with 10 generations per intent) on AdvBench with the highest diversity score among all compared methods, which is 2.1x that of the strongest-attacking baseline. The resulting attacks transfer to unseen frontier LLMs, reaching 71.0% ASR@10 on AdvBench with the unseen victim Claude-Opus-4.6. The code will be released.
papers.title_zh: CoFiBreak：用于有效多轮越狱的由粗到细多样性奖励
papers.abstract_zh: 自动化红队训练一个攻击者大语言模型（LLM）以诱导受害者 LLM 产生有害回应，但当攻击成功是唯一奖励时，强化学习可能使攻击者坍缩到一组狭窄的提示上。这种攻击多样性的坍缩可能使安全评估偏向于反复测试近乎重复的攻击模式，而不是底层有害意图。现有方法常常以攻击成功率或推理成本为代价换取更大的内容或策略多样性。我们提出 CoFiBreak，一种用于组相对策略优化（GRPO）的由粗到细多样性奖励，它在保持强攻击有效性和低推理成本的同时提高攻击多样性。粗粒度奖励通过鼓励每个 GRPO 组内代表性不足的策略，拓宽攻击者使用的策略；细粒度奖励则通过在从提示嵌入中移除有害意图信息后抑制对相同角色、框架和输出格式的重复使用，拓宽这些策略的实现方式。多样性奖励仅适用于已经超过有效性阈值的攻击，因此不能通过无效攻击获得多样性。由于两种奖励仅在训练期间计算，CoFiBreak 还保留了推理效率。以 Llama3.1-8B-Instruct 作为受害者模型进行训练，CoFiBreak 在 HarmBench 上跨前沿受害者模型发现的不同的成功细粒度策略数量是最强基线的 1.6–2.0 倍。它在 AdvBench 上达到 98.8% ASR@10（每个意图生成 10 次时的攻击成功率），并在所有比较方法中取得最高多样性得分，该得分是最强攻击基线的 2.1 倍。所得攻击可迁移到未见的前沿 LLM，在 AdvBench 上以未见受害者 Claude-Opus-4.6 达到 71.0% ASR@10。代码将发布。

papers.title: Adaptive Personalization Under Preference Epistemic Uncertainty
papers.summary: Human preferences change over time: an established preference may remain valid over time, become uncertain as context shifts, or be explicitly revised. Effective personalization requires conversational AI to adapt its response strategy to evolving preferences rather than relying on passive memory retrieval. We formalize this capability as adaptive personalization under epistemic uncertainty. A human preference study further confirms that people favor state-contingent response strategies as preference uncertainty changes. To evaluate whether language models mirror this adaptation, we create a multilingual benchmark spanning 250 personas, 5 languages, and 25K conversational turns that decouples strategy selection from response execution. Across eight closed- and open-weight models, we uncover a recognition-generation gap: models reliably identify appropriate strategies when selecting among candidate options, but collapse during open-ended generation, suffering a 35-46% drop in strategy calibration. Crucially, this failure is systematic: models default to exploit-first behavior, over-relying on existing preferences regardless of preference epistemic uncertainty. We show this failure is addressable: while prompting interventions fail, targeted training that supervises models' internal strategy representations toward state-conditional human preferences narrows the user acceptability generalization gap by a third on out-of-distribution personas and conversational styles.

papers.title: Better Retrievers, Worse Labels: How Incomplete Relevance Judgments Distort Abstention Evaluation in Conversational RAG
papers.summary: Conversational RAG benchmarks such as MTRAG and RETECO evaluate retrieval and generation end to end: each system answers from its own retrieval, so abstention must be scored against whether each retrieved context is sufficient. A convenient shortcut reads sufficiency off the relevance judgments and treats a context without gold documents as unanswerable. We re-run the official baselines exactly and test this shortcut on RECOR (RETECO track~2) with four retrievers (nDCG@10 from .18 to .59) and three Qwen3 readers. Two open LLM judges and a panel of four small open models label each context by content, and a model of another family audits 250 contexts blind, with adjudication. The stronger the retriever, the larger the share of no-gold contexts that still contain the answer (28\% to 72\%) and the lower the shortcut's precision (.68 to .10; .70 to .21 under the audit). A reader agrees: Qwen3-4B answers 62--67\% of these false misses correctly, against 23--30\% of no-gold contexts judged insufficient and 1\% with no documents. In most false misses, the answer comes from a hard negative mined for the same question, another turn's gold or a neighbouring chunk of the gold page. On MTRAG, whose judgments come from annotators, precision drops from .72 to .50. Under the shortcut, answerability AUROC is up to .19 too low, and the best sufficiency detector appears to be a retrieval score that never reads the documents. We release code, runs and labels, and recommend scoring refusals against content labels, not the presence of gold.

papers.title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
papers.summary: Large language models have been shown to memorise and reproduce verbatim sequences from their training data, raising concerns about privacy leakage, intellectual property exposure, and the limits of generalisation. Recent theoretical work suggests that attention heads may contribute to this behaviour by functioning as associative memory mechanisms, with memorisation capacity scaling with the number of heads. At the same time, empirical work has shown that many attention heads are redundant and can be pruned with limited impact on downstream performance. Despite these parallel findings, the effect of pruning redundant heads on memorised-sequence reproduction remains unexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that zeroing out a substantial fraction of attention heads prior to inference can significantly suppress verbatim memorisation while preserving, or even improving, language modelling performance on the benchmark used to identify redundant heads. Evaluating GPT-2-XL(1.5B) on known memorised sequences, we find that pruning 729 task-redundant heads reduces the memorisation count by 91.5%, while improving WikiText-103 perplexity by 0.92. These findings suggest that attention-head redundancy can be exploited to mitigate memorisation at inference time, without retraining or modifying the training data.
papers.title_zh: 更少的头，更少的记忆：剪枝冗余注意力头可抑制逐字记忆
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型已被证明会记忆并逐字复现其训练数据中的序列，这引发了对隐私泄露、知识产权暴露以及泛化能力局限的担忧。近期的理论工作表明，注意力头可能通过充当联想记忆机制而为这一行为作出贡献，且记忆容量随注意力头数量的增加而扩展。与此同时，实证工作已表明，许多注意力头是冗余的，剪枝它们对下游性能的影响有限。尽管存在这些并行的发现，剪枝冗余注意力头对已记忆序列复现的影响仍未被探索。在本工作中，我们证明，在推理之前将相当大一部分注意力头置零，可以显著抑制逐字记忆，同时在用于识别冗余头的基准上保持甚至提升语言建模性能。在已知的已记忆序列上评估 GPT-2-XL(1.5B)，我们发现剪枝 729 个任务冗余注意力头使记忆计数降低 91.5%，同时将 WikiText-103 困惑度改善 0.92。这些发现表明，可以利用注意力头的冗余性在推理时缓解记忆，而无需重新训练或修改训练数据。

papers.title: Do Open Language Models Invent Scripture? BILAL-BENCH: Benchmarking Islamic-Source Fabrication in Bengali
papers.summary: When a language model invents a Qur'anic verse or hadith, it gives false authority to text that readers may treat as sacred. Existing Islamic hallucination benchmarks are largely Arabic and often closed-ended, while Bengali resources mainly study general-domain hallucination or factual knowledge. We introduce BILAL-BENCH, a 240-question expert-verified benchmark for open-ended Islamic-source fabrication in Bengali. It covers Qur'anic attribution, hadith, fiqh, contemporary issues, and adversarial false-premise prompts, and uses a two-axis rubric that separates source errors from assertiveness. We evaluate seven open-weight models from 1B to 120B on 1,680 double-annotated responses. Six of the seven models confidently fabricate on 79.3-95.3% of source-production questions, with no monotonic improvement from scale. Hadith provenance is the weakest category across models: only two of 315 responses are correct and correctly sourced. The two 8B BanglaLLaMA variants have similar confident-fabrication rates but different error profiles. Models vary far more in whether they withhold a claim they cannot support than in source accuracy: appropriate abstention or false-premise correction ranges from 6 to 46 responses across the benchmark, and does not track parameter count.

papers.title: Language Models Show Conformity Bias in RAG: When the Majority Endorses a Poisoned Claim
papers.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can expose language models to misleading evidence in retrieved documents. We investigate whether increasing the number of mutually agreeing poisoned documents affects a model's ability to detect misinformation. We evaluate 200 randomly selected questions from SciFact (random seed 38), comparing contexts with one poisoned and six healthy documents against contexts with six mutually agreeing poisoned documents and one healthy document. For Gemma-3-12b, poison-detection rates decrease from 25% (50/200) in the minority condition to 10% (20/200) in the majority condition. Among the 38 questions with different outcomes across conditions, 34 change from detected to undetected, while only four change in the opposite direction (exact McNemar test, p = 6.04e-7). This pattern is consistent with a conformity-like response to a majority of mutually agreeing poisoned documents. Our results provide initial evidence of conformity bias in RAG-based misinformation detection: Gemma-3-12b is substantially less likely to detect poisoned claims when they dominate the retrieved evidence.

papers.title: EDU-Jev Training System-One Decision Models for Education
papers.summary: Many automated decisions in education involve choosing from a fixed set of options: assigning a rubric score, checking whether an answer meets a marking criterion, or identifying the first wrong step in a solution. Generative language models are increasingly used to make these decisions, but their responses require parsing, longer outputs increase inference costs, and confidence expressed in words does not necessarily reflect the probability of being correct. We present EDU-Jev, a family of single-pass ("System One") decision models at 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameters. Given an assessment context and a question with predefined answer options, the model returns a probability distribution over those options without generating text. A pointer head scores a marker for each option, ensuring the predictions are restricted to the allowed choices. Training uses a single supervised stage with soft cross-entropy against the available target label distributions; calibration is assessed empirically. Across twelve education benchmarks, EDU-Jev 4B achieves an average accuracy of 67.6%, exceeding the strongest of five commercial decision APIs by 9.4 percentage points and the best open 4B decision model by 18.7 points. On four cross-domain education sets, it matches the strongest API, which remains ahead on general decision-making and reasoning tasks. The 2B model processes about 150 decisions per second on a single H100 GPU.

papers.title: Language Models Show a "Women-Are-Wonderful" Effect in Blame Attribution That is Not Just Leniency
papers.summary: This paper investigates the Women-Are-Wonderful (WaW) effect in language-model blame attribution: a favorable bias in which women receive more positive evaluations than men. Using 11,270 interpersonal conflicts from r/AmItheAsshole, we construct matched counterfactuals that vary the gender of the person being judged (the original poster) and the person affected (the counter-party). Across four language models, gender changes a minority of verdicts, but those changes consistently favor women. The effect is strongly role-dependent. Making the original poster a woman reduces the odds of blame by 9--52%, while making the counter-party a woman multiplies them by 2.7--9.2X. Counter-party WaW also varies across conflict types, strengthening in communication and relationship conflicts and weakening in family conflicts. Exploratory probes suggest that counter-party gender can shift judgments of sympathy, reasonableness, harm and protection. WaW is therefore not just leniency toward women being judged: models also judge conduct more harshly when it affects a woman.

papers.title: HyperRepair: Recovering Forgotten General Capabilities of Fine-Tuned Language Models
papers.summary: Fine-tuning improves a language model's performance in a target domain but can weaken its general capabilities. Existing methods often face a trade-off between general capabilities and domain specialization, making it difficult to preserve both. We introduce HyperRepair, a framework for recovering general capabilities while retaining domain specialization at only inference cost. To make recovery generalizable across models sharing a pretrained backbone, HyperRepair learns a hypernetwork from repairs trained on source models. The hypernetwork uses activation fingerprints that summarize changes from the pretrained backbone to generate a tailored Repairing Side Net (RSN), whose prompt-conditioned gate applies corrections selectively. This enables recovery on models from unseen adaptation domains without target-domain examples or additional optimization. We evaluate HyperRpair across two model families, 12 LoRA adaptation datasets, and 15 general benchmarks. On the default split, HyperRepair achieves 93.4% of the base models' average general score while retaining 99.5% of the fine-tuned models' average domain score.

papers.title: S2TDR: Structured Multimodal Reconstruction for Sticker-Aware Dialogue Understanding
papers.summary: Stickers are widely used in social media dialogues to express affect, stance, and intent beyond literal text. Their meanings are often non-literal and context-dependent, making them difficult to handle with generic visual fusion or standalone captioning. We propose Sticker-to-Text Dialogue Reconstruction (S2TDR), a structured multimodal reconstruction framework that converts sticker turns into contextually appropriate textual utterances. S2TDR decomposes sticker interpretation into visual cue extraction, affective-intent inference, and context-aware dialogue reconstruction, using OCR text only as an auxiliary cue when available. The reconstructed dialogue can then be consumed by existing text-based dialogue models. Experiments on sentiment analysis, intent recognition, and dialogue summarization show that S2TDR generally improves multiple downstream models over direct sticker integration methods. Further analyses on component ablations, OCR-empty stickers, and reconstruction quality indicate that structured reconstruction provides an interpretable and effective way to integrate sticker semantics into dialogue understanding.

papers.title: TraceSpec: Understanding and Improving Speculative Decoding for LLM Agents
papers.summary: LLM agents execute tasks through repeated model calls over evolving histories of reasoning, actions, and tool feedback. Aggregate speculative-decoding metrics merge these distinct decisions, providing limited guidance on where draft supervision is needed. We present TraceSpec, a framework connecting trajectory evaluation with adaptive draft training. It combines dynamic execution with fixed-prefix replay and introduces TraceSpec-Traj, a corpus of 10,000 training states and 2,500 test states spanning browsing and software engineering. Analysis of five speculative baselines reveals that aggregate acceptance can rise with context length while declining within matched late browsing actions. Workload and phase further distinguish these trends, motivating supervision guided by trajectory conditions. TraceSpec trains on intermediate assistant turns and allocates a fixed prediction budget using state-conditioned estimates of prefix-aware acceptance gaps. Across three target sizes and two temperatures, it improves replay throughput by 12.5% to 22.6% over its DSpark base. Qwen3-4B ablations show that adaptive allocation increases accepted length by 3.3% to 10.0% over fixed full-turn supervision, with additional comparisons substantiating the roles of state conditioning and consecutive-token agreement. The resulting evaluation resources, trajectory findings, and training strategy connect the analysis of agent execution to practical draft improvement.

papers.title: Beyond Response Scoring: An AI-aware Cognitive Supervision Framework for Automated Mathematical Short Answer Grading
papers.summary: Transformer-based language models have achieved remarkable success in automated short answer grading (ASAG). However, current methods in ASAG struggle to comprehend, reason about and evaluate complex mathematical answers involving symbols and formulas. These score-only methods fail to generalize across diverse responses and skill states associated with identical scores. Moreover, they ignore the potential upward bias introduced by generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage in assessing students' performance and knowledge mastery. To address these limitations, we propose AICG (AI-aware Cognitive-supervised Grading), a two-branch multi-task framework. The first branch combines RoBERTa-based regression, ordinal, and classification heads for individual-answer grading. The second branch uses an expert-designed Q-matrix to associate responses with assessed skills and jointly predicts G-DINA-derived skill mastery and learning gain. Through the shared encoder, these skill-level targets provide cognitive supervision for answer grading beyond score labels. AICG further uses a Gen-AI detector, trained through supervised contrastive pretraining followed by linear classification, to estimate assistance probabilities and convert them into reliability weights, attenuating unreliable cognitive evidence during learning assessment. We conduct experiments on 49,402 instructor-graded responses spanning 19 academic semesters. Relative to RoBERTa regression, AICG reduces mean absolute error (MAE) by 50.3% and improves quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) from 0.798 to 0.927. Ablations identify Q-matrix-guided cognitive supervision as the primary source of improvement, while AI-aware weighting further reduces overall MAE by 4.2% over the unweighted cognitive model and consistently improves MAE and QWK across the four most recent post-Gen-AI semesters.

papers.title: PsyInterviewee: Informational Invariance and Relational Adaptivity in Mental Health Interview Simulation
papers.summary: LLM-based simulated interviewees support interviewer training and the evaluation of mental health interviewing systems. Existing studies have primarily focused on improving human-likeness through richer patient profiles and behavioral modeling. However, human-likeness alone does not establish their reliability. Reliable simulation requires preserving profile-grounded clinical facts (informational invariance) while adapting disclosure and interaction behavior to the interview (relational adaptivity). To this end, we introduce PsyInterviewee, which separates a protected truth channel from a dynamic interaction channel and verifies generated clinical claims against the profile. Specifically, asymmetric write permissions allow dialogue context to update disclosure and behavioral states without authorizing new clinical facts; these states guide what profile-supported information is revealed and how it is expressed. In an automated evaluation of interactions between LLM-based interviewers and interviewees, PsyInterviewee achieves higher scores than four representative baselines on most metrics across both axes, as assessed by two LLM judges. Ablations suggest that the two channels contribute to clinical grounding and response modulation, respectively.

papers.title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents play an important role in solving complex and sustained tasks, with ever-growing interaction contexts. However, these accumulated contexts will raise substantial computational cost and obscure key decision-relevant evidence. Existing methods typically train external compressors or context-management agents to rewrite context as shorter hard-token sequences, but such external selection may not align with the LLM's evolving representation and is necessarily lossy. In this paper, we introduce Agentic Soft-Token Compression (ASTC), a training-free compression method using soft tokens within LLM agent for long-horizon tasks. Specifically, ASTC uses the model's native recurrent dynamics to determine the already absorbed information, leveraging the commonly-used hybrid Gated Delta Network (GDN)-attention. It then carries this information forward as agentic soft tokens while retaining exact values as hard tokens. The resulting compact sequence reduces later-layer computation and yields reusable KV caches, extending the savings across the agent's trajectory. Extensive experiments on long-horizon tasks show that ASTC matches or exceeds the uncompressed agent's accuracy with up to 50.68% fewer end-to-end Attention Pairs, while trained compressors require 15.4 to 103.7 times more Attention Pairs per successful task. These findings highlight agentic soft tokens as a model-native way to carry absorbed context forward as the task representation evolves.

papers.title: From Transcription to Reformulation: Defining and Benchmarking Grounded Generative Speech Recognition
papers.summary: Speech language models have expanded automatic speech recognition (ASR) from transcription to general speech-to-text generation. Yet existing benchmarks still assume a single ground-truth transcript per utterance, an assumption that struggles when models produce readable, formatted, or structured outputs. In this work, we introduce Grounded Generative Speech Recognition (GSR), reformulating speech recognition as generating semantically grounded text instead of a single transcript. We define a grounded reformulation space that characterizes all valid textual realizations supported by the input speech, and establish a four-level hierarchy of reformulation capabilities, including literal transcription, canonical reformulation, semantic reformulation and speech-grounded structuring. Based on this formulation, we present GSR-Bench, the first comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate generative speech recognition systems beyond exact transcript matching. GSR-Bench covers diverse scenarios including refined meeting transcription, cross-dialect translation, context-aware speech understanding, and robustness under silent or noisy acoustic conditions. To address the limitations of word-level evaluation metrics, we develop a multi-dimensional evaluation framework combining speech grounding assessment and LLM-based semantic judgment, whose reliability is validated through human preference studies. Extensive experiments across representative architectures, ranging from conventional ASR systems to end-to-end Speech-LLMs, reveal fundamental trade-offs between transcription fidelity and generative reformulation ability. Our analysis further identifies critical failure modes, including acoustic hallucination, unsupported generation, and instruction drift, providing insights into the design and evaluation of future grounded generative speech systems.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Based Review Paradigms for Academic Paper Quality Assessment
papers.summary: Growing submission volumes have renewed interest in using large language models (LLMs) to support peer review. It remains unclear how such evaluation should be structured, how much the model matters, and whether LLM scores predict research impact. We evaluate five paradigms across three input representations and three LLMs on 232 stratified ICLR 2025 submissions. Direct absolute rating matches comparative ranking on rank correlation with human scores, yet compresses most predictions above the accept threshold, flagging almost none of the papers reviewers scored below it. A base-rate-matched recalibration control locates the cause: comparative ranking supplies placement, not better ordering, and after recalibration Direct Rating reaches higher agreement than Elo while making 24% as many API calls. Abstract-only input beats full-paper summarization, and model choice matters as much as paradigm choice. Replicating on all 11,513 scored submissions reproduces these patterns, shows absolute agreement depends on the evaluated set's score spread, and finds none beating an always-reject baseline in accuracy. Human scores track citations better than any paradigm, with one exception: Group Rating retains its citation correlation after controlling for human scores, and alone ranks within the accepted pool. Ranking quality alone cannot assess review quality; calibration, thresholds, model, and target outcome all matter.
papers.title_zh: 基于LLM的学术论文质量评估评审范式的比较评价
papers.abstract_zh: 不断增长的投稿量重新激起了使用大语言模型（LLM）支持同行评审的兴趣。目前仍不清楚此类评估应如何组织、模型本身有多重要，以及LLM评分是否能预测研究影响力。我们在232篇分层抽样的ICLR 2025投稿上，跨三种输入表示和三个LLM评估了五种范式。直接绝对评分在与人类评分的秩相关上与比较排序相当，但会将大多数预测压缩到接收阈值以上，几乎未能标记出任何审稿人评分低于该阈值的论文。一个与基础率匹配的重校准对照定位了原因：比较排序提供的是位置放置，而非更好的排序；经过重校准后，Direct Rating达到的一致性高于Elo，同时API调用量仅为其24%。仅摘要输入优于全文摘要输入，且模型选择与范式选择同等重要。在全部11,513篇有评分的投稿上复现实验重现了这些模式，表明绝对一致性取决于被评估集合的分数分布范围，并发现没有任何方法在准确率上优于始终拒绝的基线。人类评分对引用量的追踪优于任何范式，但有一个例外：Group Rating在控制人类评分后仍保留其与引用量的相关性，并且是唯一能在接收论文池内进行排序的方法。仅凭排序质量无法评估评审质量；校准、阈值、模型和目标结果都至关重要。

papers.title: BlindToChange: AI Agents Can Find Changes When Asked But Do They Look When Needed?
papers.summary: Given that AI agents can search the web broadly and deeply in real time, it is tempting to conclude that their outputs account for recent world events. We show that this conclusion does not hold in practice. While agents can search and easily find recent changes, the correctness of their responses depends on whether they search and what they search for. Popular agentic search benchmarks like BrowseComp cannot expose failures wherein agents do not recognize their own assumptions that should be verified, since these benchmarks explicitly state what needs to be found. In contrast, many user requests state only the final information need (e.g., an itinerary for a trip), leaving the agent to discover relevant changes (e.g., the temporary closure of a museum) and account for their consequences. To highlight such gaps, we introduce BlindToChange, a benchmark that measures whether agents proactively discover recent events that affect their responses. Our benchmark comprises requests for recommendations where an obvious candidate is no longer applicable due to a recent real-world event. These events are drawn automatically from Wikidata, allowing BlindToChange to be periodically refreshed. Strikingly, we find a big gap -- as high as 27.5 points, even at high reasoning effort -- in systems' performance, when the recent event is not explicitly mentioned compared to when we ask about it directly. Analyzing search trajectories, we learn that more than half of the failures can be attributed to the fact that agents do not directly search to verify whether a relevant fact has changed. Our benchmark highlights, and tracks, a new axis of progress, wherein systems account for recent information that is not explicitly mentioned in the user request.

papers.title: KV-Cache Patching: Tracing How and Where Fine-Tuned Behaviors Arise
papers.summary: Fine-tuning a language model changes how it responds, but where is this fine-tuned behavior instantiated? To better understand this, we evaluate whether the change in model behavior arises only during the generation of the answer tokens where the change manifests, or whether altered processing of previous tokens causes it via the attention mechanism. For this, we patch the KV cache from a LoRA fine-tuned model into the unmodified base model, and vice versa. Our results show that for some behaviors, like responding in German or emergent misalignment, patching the KV cache can indeed transfer them from the fine-tuned to the base model. Correspondingly, patching the KV cache from base to fine-tune can partially or fully remove fine-tuned behavior. Furthermore, we find that the effect of patching grows with how much of the KV cache is patched and concentrates at a few pivotal positions, with system-prompt and chat-template tokens having disproportionate influence.

papers.title: KEEPER: Learning Control-Sufficient Textual Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.summary: Recursive textual memory can carry earlier errors into later updates, yet task performance alone does not establish memory reliability. We define self-consistency bias as the persistence of incorrect claims already present in the incoming memory. We present KEEPER, a comparative analysis of four auxiliary objectives along information-content and update-sensitivity axes within a shared recursive interface, examining how supervision targets relate to agent performance. Among evaluated conditions, reward-related prediction achieve the highest task performance before and after offline reinforcement learning, outperforming joint supervision. A claim-level analysis of one baseline trajectory documents error persistence despite corrective observations. Together, these analyses motivate evaluating error persistence and valid-information retention alongside task outcomes.

papers.title: Sparse Text Diffusion under Dual Budgets: Context Connectivity and Expert Activation
papers.summary: Long-context diffusion repeatedly pays for both token interaction and feed-forward computation. We formulate these costs as two separate budgets: the edges available to an attention graph and the experts activated for each token. This view connects local, dilated, and global attention with conditional expert computation without assuming that sparsity alone preserves document-level information. We specify normalized masked attention, distinguish denoising depth from sampling iterations, and derive graph and compute bounds. A reported sparse-expert configuration, denoted DualBudget, is analyzed across scientific summarization, multi-hop question answering, dialogue, and sentence-pair prediction. All supplied table measurements are retained. The length study shows gains over the listed baselines through 16K, together with measurable degradation as length increases. Ablations reveal mixed changes across the three reported scores, while the cost record indicates a 20% reduction relative to DiffuSeq under an unspecified timing convention. The analysis separates these observations from unmeasured claims about training speed, absorbing states, global coherence, and deployment memory.
papers.title_zh: 双重预算下的稀疏文本扩散：上下文连通性与专家激活
papers.abstract_zh: 长上下文扩散会反复为 token 交互和前馈计算付出代价。我们将这些成本表述为两个独立的预算：注意力图可用的边，以及每个 token 所激活的专家。这一视角将局部注意力、膨胀注意力和全局注意力与条件专家计算联系起来，而不假设仅靠稀疏性就能保留文档级信息。我们指定了归一化掩码注意力，区分了去噪深度与采样迭代，并推导了图与计算的上界。一个被报告的稀疏专家配置，记为 DualBudget，在科学摘要、多跳问答、对话和句子对预测任务上进行了分析。所有提供的表格测量值均被保留。长度研究表明，在截至 16K 的范围内相对于所列基线有所提升，同时随着长度增加也出现了可测量的退化。消融实验揭示了三个所报告分数上的混合变化，而成本记录表明，在未指定的计时约定下，相对于 DiffuSeq 降低了 20%。该分析将这些观察结果与关于训练速度、吸收态、全局连贯性和部署内存的未测量主张区分开来。

papers.title: Enhancing Knowledge Entity Relation Extraction in Abstracts and Full-text Content of Academic Articles Using Large Language Models
papers.summary: This study investigates the effectiveness of large pre-trained language models (LLMs) for knowledge entity relation extraction (KERE) from academic papers. Existing studies have examined individual types of LLM-based strategies and evaluated model performance using metrics such as precision and recall. To provide a broader evaluation, this study investigates multiple strategies, including closed-source LLM-based CoT prompting, LoRA-adapted open-source LLMs, LLM-enhanced small pre-trained language models (SLMs), and SLM-enhanced closed-source LLMs. In addition, this study introduces two strategies, namely SLM-enhanced open-source LLMs and closed-source LLM-enhanced open-source LLMs. These strategies are evaluated from multiple perspectives, including metrics, their ability to mitigate errors observed in SLMs, and potential directions for model optimization. This study manually constructs two annotated datasets in the NLP domain, covering Abstract and Full-Text datasets. Experimental results show that the LoRA-adapted T5 model achieves the highest macro F1 scores of 0.7408 and 0.7013 on the Abstract and Full-Text datasets, respectively. SLMs also benefit from LLM-generated entity descriptions under the LLM-enhanced SLM strategy. Error analysis further reveals that the effectiveness of LLM-based strategies in mitigating SLM errors varies across error types. Based on the identified limitations and error patterns of these strategies, several optimization directions are proposed. In addition, combining strategies with different error patterns further improves KERE performance.
papers.title_zh: 利用大型语言模型增强学术文章摘要和全文内容中的知识实体关系抽取
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究考察了大型预训练语言模型（LLMs）在从学术论文中抽取知识实体关系（KERE）方面的有效性。已有研究考察了单一类型的基于LLM的策略，并使用精确率和召回率等指标评估模型性能。为了提供更广泛的评估，本研究考察了多种策略，包括基于闭源LLM的CoT提示、LoRA适配的开源LLM、LLM增强的小型预训练语言模型（SLMs）以及SLM增强的闭源LLM。此外，本研究引入了两种策略，即SLM增强的开源LLM和闭源LLM增强的开源LLM。这些策略从多个角度进行评估，包括指标、它们缓解在SLM中观察到的错误的能力，以及模型优化的潜在方向。本研究在NLP领域人工构建了两个标注数据集，涵盖摘要数据集和全文数据集。实验结果表明，LoRA适配的T5模型在摘要数据集和全文数据集上分别取得了最高的宏F1分数0.7408和0.7013。在LLM增强SLM策略下，SLM也受益于LLM生成的实体描述。错误分析进一步表明，基于LLM的策略在缓解SLM错误方面的有效性因错误类型而异。基于这些策略已识别的局限性和错误模式，提出了若干优化方向。此外，将具有不同错误模式的策略相结合进一步提高了KERE性能。

papers.title: CEFR Level Assessment across Languages and Text Granularities
papers.summary: Automatic assessment of textual CEFR levels is an important task in educational natural language processing. However, accurate CEFR level prediction remains challenging due to the naturally imbalanced distribution of CEFR levels and the ambiguous boundaries between adjacent levels. To address these challenges, we propose a unified training objective that combines focal loss with supervised contrastive learning. Focal loss mitigates class imbalance by emphasizing underrepresented and difficult examples, while supervised contrastive learning learns more discriminative representations by encouraging intra-class compactness and inter-class separation. We evaluate the proposed method on sentence- and document-level CEFR assessment in both monolingual and multilingual settings. Experimental results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms strong baselines across all settings, establishing new state-of-the-art performance on multiple CEFR assessment benchmarks.

papers.title: Digital sovereignty in professional translation workflows: a case study of migrating from Windows to Linux
papers.summary: This study examines digital sovereignty in professional translation through a screening of computer-assisted translation tools and translation management systems, and a case study of migrating a translator's workstation from Windows to Linux. The framework combines three principles - Control, Continuity and Exit - with three practical requirements: native Linux operation, independence from mandatory external services, and independent access to essential data and resources. Drawing on documentary evidence and the limited number of responses received from providers, the ecosystem screening distinguishes Linux accessibility from operational independence: browser-based platforms may remain dependent on provider-controlled infrastructure. The migration case demonstrates the feasibility of reconstructing one professional workflow around a locally operable Linux core, using LoopCAT, LibreOffice and locally run TranslateGemma, alongside tools for optical character recognition, communication, credential management and backup. Selected cloud services remained available where needed. The findings suggest that digital sovereignty depends on how workflow dependencies are organized, rather than on individual applications or operating systems. It does not require technological isolation, but meaningful control over essential components, continuity of work and practical exit options. The framework is tailored to the case examined here and may require adaptation to other professional workflows.

papers.title: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion
papers.summary: Unlike autoregressive (AR) models, diffusion language models (DLMs) permit parallel token updates, flexible generation, and bidirectional attention, but leading systems rely on costly pretraining or full-model fine-tuning. We present Build Your Own DLM (BYOD), a generalizable LoRA-only recipe for parameter-efficient AR-to-DLM conversion. Without architecture-specific tuning, BYOD induces diffusion generation in Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B, and Ministral 8B; to our knowledge, this is the first reported AR-to-DLM conversion of a Mistral model. The adapters comprise 4.1-5.8% of final parameters while every base-model parameter remains frozen; each 25,000-iteration conversion needs at most 102.4M tokens, processed in 3.1-4.0 hours on one Google Colab GPU. All four models generate from fully masked sequences, use bidirectional context in a controlled attention test, and retain substantial parent-model knowledge. BYOD-Gemma is the strongest BYOD conversion on our nine-task evaluation, reaching 50.6% average accuracy compared with 51.9% for LLaDA 8B Instruct in the same harness. Open-generation quality at low network function evaluation (NFE) budgets remains the principal limitation: BYOD perplexity is 8.3-11.1 versus 4.1 for LLaDA and 2.2-3.0 for the AR parents when generating 128 tokens in 64 steps. To enable further experimentation and inspection, we provide a standalone training and evaluation implementation and interactive demos for all four conversions. BYOD thus provides a practical route for extending diffusion generation to other existing model families while identifying the gap that efficient conversion must next close.
papers.title_zh: BYOD：构建你自己的 DLM——高效的自回归到扩散语言模型转换
papers.abstract_zh: 与自回归（AR）模型不同，扩散语言模型（DLM）允许并行 token 更新、灵活生成和双向注意力，但领先的系统依赖于昂贵的预训练或全模型微调。我们提出 Build Your Own DLM（BYOD），一种可泛化的、仅使用 LoRA 的配方，用于参数高效的 AR 到 DLM 转换。无需针对架构的调优，BYOD 在 Gemma 2 9B、Llama 3.1 8B、Qwen2.5 7B 和 Ministral 8B 中诱导出扩散生成；据我们所知，这是首次报道的 Mistral 模型的 AR 到 DLM 转换。适配器占最终参数的 4.1-5.8%，而每个基础模型参数都保持冻结；每次 25,000 次迭代的转换至多需要 1.024 亿个 token，在一张 Google Colab GPU 上处理耗时 3.1-4.0 小时。所有四个模型都能从完全掩码的序列生成，在受控注意力测试中使用双向上下文，并保留大量父模型知识。在我们的九项任务评估中，BYOD-Gemma 是最强的 BYOD 转换，达到 50.6% 的平均准确率，而在同一评测框架中 LLaDA 8B Instruct 为 51.9%。低网络函数评估（NFE）预算下的开放生成质量仍是主要限制：在 64 步内生成 128 个 token 时，BYOD 的困惑度为 8.3-11.1，而 LLaDA 为 4.1，AR 父模型为 2.2-3.0。为支持进一步的实验和检视，我们提供了独立的训练与评估实现，以及所有四种转换的交互式演示。因此，BYOD 为将扩散生成扩展到其他现有模型家族提供了一条实用路径，同时指出了高效转换接下来必须弥合的差距。

papers.title: Saidzoda-Tajik-LFM-2.6B: Adapting a 2.6B Hybrid Model to Tajik Tool Calling, and What Continued Pretraining Takes Away
papers.summary: We release Saidzoda-Tajik-LFM-2.6B, a Tajik adaptation of the 2.6B-parameter hybrid model LFM2.5-2.6B-Base, built for tool calling in Tajik on modest hardware. The recipe has two stages: LoRA continued pretraining (CPT) on 1,485,319 cleaned Tajik web documents for 3 epochs, then one epoch of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a mix of machine-translated Tajik tool calls, English tool calls kept as replay, and Tajik instructions. On a 174-item tool-calling test set built from BFCL v3 and machine-translated to Tajik, strict full-call accuracy on Tajik prompts rises from 20.69 for the base model to 64.14 (paired difference +43.45 points, 95% interval +35.2 to +51.7); a lenient parser that also accepts the base model's own call formats puts the base at 31.72. English shows no detectable change (76.55 and 77.24). Every CPT checkpoint scores zero: CPT removes the native tool-call format and, as the lenient re-scoring shows, part of the skill itself. Outside tool calling, accuracy on a Tajik knowledge benchmark rises from 28.0 to 35.0, Belebele Tajik shows no significant change, and English MMLU falls from 60.8 to 52.5. The model is not a general Tajik assistant. It almost never declines when no tool fits (6.9% correct on Tajik, against 31.0% for the base under the lenient parser), it is weak at multi-turn calls, and its calls should be checked before they are executed. We describe the data, the training settings and every evaluation in enough detail to repeat them.

papers.title: When Steering Shifts Discourse: Identifying and Intervening on Discourse-Level Changes due to Activation Steering in LLMs
papers.summary: Activation steering is an inference-time technique used to control or modify the behavior, tone, or safety properties of a large language model (LLM) without retraining the model's weights or editing its input prompt, but simply by adding a vector to its residual-stream activations. However, activation steering also changes the generated text in unintended ways, unrelated to intended behavior change, that are not well understood. Prior work has measured these changes only through coarse signals such as perplexity. In this work, we show that steering systematically produces significant changes in discourse dimensions of the generated text, such as its formality, use of evidence, and ambiguity. We present a way of countering this by adding a second, complementary vector that targets the affected discourse dimension. This intervention restores about 78% of the unintended discourse changes while preserving the intended steering behavior in about 93% of the generations.
papers.title_zh: 当引导改变话语：识别并干预大语言模型中由激活引导引起的话语层面变化
papers.abstract_zh: 激活引导是一种推理时技术，用于控制或修改大语言模型（LLM）的行为、语气或安全属性，其无需重新训练模型权重或编辑输入提示，而只需向其残差流激活中加入一个向量。然而，激活引导也会以与预期行为改变无关的、尚未被充分理解的意外方式改变生成的文本。先前的工作仅通过诸如困惑度之类的粗略信号来衡量这些变化。在本工作中，我们表明引导会系统性地使生成文本的话语维度产生显著变化，例如其正式程度、证据使用和歧义性。我们提出了一种通过加入第二个互补向量来应对这一问题的方法，该向量针对受影响的话语维度。这种干预恢复了约 78% 的意外话语变化，同时在约 93% 的生成中保留了预期的引导行为。

papers.title: Precision--Recall Trade-off on the Inference Level for LLMs in Grammatical Error Correction
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have recently been adopted for Grammatical Error Correction (GEC), achieving strong performance via both full fine-tuning and prompt-based approaches. As probabilistic sequence models, LLMs expose inference-time parameters that directly modify token generation behavior; however, their potential for controlling GEC-specific trade-offs has not been systematically studied. In this work, we investigate decoding strategies for grammatical error correction. We show that the repetition penalty parameter enables controllable adjustment of the precision--recall trade-off at inference time, without modifying the model architecture, training procedure, or prompt. Through experiments on standard GEC benchmarks, we demonstrate that repetition-penalty-based decoding enables inference-time control of the precision--recall balance, conceptually related to methods previously proposed for sequence-to-sequence GEC models, such as Align-and-Predict Decoding (APD), while remaining simple and broadly applicable to existing LLMs that expose inference-time decoding penalties.
papers.title_zh: 语法错误纠正中大型语言模型在推理层面的精确率--召回率权衡
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）最近已被用于语法错误纠正（GEC），通过全参数微调和基于提示的方法均取得了强劲的性能。作为概率序列模型，LLMs 暴露了一些推理时参数，这些参数可以直接改变词元生成行为；然而，它们在控制 GEC 特定权衡方面的潜力尚未得到系统研究。在本工作中，我们研究用于语法错误纠正的解码策略。我们表明，重复惩罚参数能够在推理时实现对精确率--召回率权衡的可控调节，而无需修改模型架构、训练过程或提示。通过在标准 GEC 基准上的实验，我们证明基于重复惩罚的解码能够在推理时控制精确率--召回率平衡，这在概念上与先前为序列到序列 GEC 模型提出的方法（如对齐与预测解码（Align-and-Predict Decoding, APD））相关，同时保持简单，并可广泛适用于暴露推理时解码惩罚的现有 LLMs。

papers.title: GraphNIAH: A Benchmark for Long-Context Reasoning over Real-World Graphs
papers.summary: The needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) benchmark was introduced as a test for measuring a model's ability to find small relevant facts within a very large body of input text. However, existing NIAH benchmarks each suffer from one or more of the following limitations: (1) reliance on synthetic data, so their evaluations may not generalize to real-world settings; (2) reuse of previously published datasets, leading to the risk of benchmark contamination; (3) dependence on manual annotation, which requires human effort to create and update data and is prone to future benchmark contamination; and (4) unrealistic simplification of long-context multi-hop reasoning where each next step is trivial given previous steps, while real-world reasoning often requires planning over multiple possible proof paths. To address these limitations, we introduce \Benchmark, a dynamic benchmark built from real citation relationships among scientific papers published after the evaluated models' knowledge cutoff date, which utilizes real-world information while ensuring no benchmark contamination. The fully automated benchmark construction pipeline samples representative subgraphs of the citation graph formed by these papers and converts each subgraph into a long-context QA example with a verifiable answer. We use GraphNIAH to evaluate eight LLMs from the GPT-5.6, Gemini-3, and Qwen3.5 families. We find that accuracy falls as questions require longer reasoning paths: at question depths of 16 and 32, the GPT-5.6 and Qwen3.5 models answer YES/NO questions no better than random guessing, mostly by answering NO; four of the eight models answer no counting example correctly, and the others model get worse as the subgraph size increases. These findings suggest that current LLMs often stop searching the citation relationships in their context before they reach the answer, even though every fact they need is in the context.

papers.title: Stepwise-Querying: Distilling Reasoning without Access to Teacher Chain-of-Thought
papers.summary: Reasoning distillation is widely used to transfer the reasoning capabilities of large language models to smaller students through teacher-generated supervision. In the black-box setting, however, teachers may expose only final answers and brief solutions, leaving intermediate calculations and validity conditions unavailable and thus limiting the reasoning supervision available for distillation. We propose Stepwise Querying, which elicits step-specific explanations without requiring access to the teacher's internal chain-of-thought (CoT) traces. Independent queries to the same teacher request intermediate derivations, validity checks, and corrections for individual steps, the assembled solutions are then used for standard supervised fine-tuning. Across two teachers, two students, and four mathematics and code benchmarks, our method achieves the highest score in 14 of 16 comparisons with three baselines. We further introduce Stepwise Explanation Information Gain (SEIG), a diagnostic based on the log-ratio of a frozen student's probabilities of correct step completion under stepwise and global explanations. Analyses on GSM8K show that incorrect-answer trajectories can remain useful when they preserve valid intermediate reasoning, while further decomposition yields limited additional gains.
papers.title_zh: 逐步查询：无需访问教师思维链的推理蒸馏
papers.abstract_zh: 推理蒸馏被广泛用于通过教师生成的监督，将大型语言模型的推理能力迁移到较小的学生模型。然而，在黑盒设置下，教师可能只暴露最终答案和简要解答，使中间计算和有效性条件不可用，从而限制了可用于蒸馏的推理监督。我们提出逐步查询（Stepwise Querying），它无需访问教师内部的思维链（CoT）轨迹，就能引出针对具体步骤的解释。对同一教师的独立查询会请求针对各个步骤的中间推导、有效性检查和纠正，随后组装得到的解答被用于标准的监督微调。在两个教师、两个学生以及四个数学和代码基准上，我们的方法在与三个基线方法的16次比较中有14次取得最高分。我们进一步引入逐步解释信息增益（Stepwise Explanation Information Gain，SEIG），这是一种基于冻结学生在逐步解释和全局解释下正确完成步骤的概率的对数比值的诊断指标。在 GSM8K 上的分析表明，当错误答案轨迹保留了有效的中间推理时，它们仍然可能有用，而进一步的分解只能带来有限的额外收益。

papers.title: Peeling the Matryoshka: Extracting Ontological Structure from Retrieval Embeddings
papers.summary: Taxonomy construction is essential for knowledge-intensive NLP yet remains costly: clustering-based methods (i) need careful per-corpus tuning and yield unstable hierarchies, while LLM-based pipelines (ii) depend on expensive task-specific training that does not transfer across domains. We report an empirical finding that bears on both: in Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) embeddings, where each leading prefix is itself a usable, coarser vector, prefix length aligns with the coarse-to-fine granularity of gold taxonomies; shuffled- and reverse-dimension controls isolate the alignment to the learned early prefix dimensions. The pattern holds across three architecturally distinct MRL models. To test whether this regularity is usable, we introduce PEEL (Peeling Embeddings to Extract Latent ontologies): a minimal probe over these frozen embeddings, trained once with an order-embedding objective that represents hierarchy as vector containment; a minimum spanning arborescence then decodes taxonomic DAGs. Using only a concept vocabulary (no documents), PEEL recovers taxonomic DAGs with high structural fidelity on two OLLM benchmarks, transferring to a new domain with no target-edge supervision. The end-to-end OLLM pipeline, which jointly discovers concepts and induces structure from document corpora, is reported as a cross-task reference. Pre-trained retrieval embeddings encode a decodable granularity gradient; a minimal probe renders it as explicit parent-child (is-a) structure.

papers.title: Iterated Integrals as Lexical Fingerprints: Path Signature Embeddings for Lexical Similarity
papers.summary: While sentence embeddings are primarily designed for semantic generalization, their latent geometry implicitly encodes surface-level lexical properties, a relationship that remains poorly understood. Shallow pooling methods discard word order, while deep Transformer models obscure these lexical alignments behind computational complexity and uninterpretable spaces. We propose constructing sentence embeddings via the path signature of Word2Vec trajectories, leveraging the iterated integrals of rough path theory to create representations that explicitly capture sequential and lexical structure in a geometrically tractable manner. Through extensive ablations spanning Word2Vec dimensions, signature depths, and PCA compression, we correlate embedding distances against five lexical string metrics: Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, word Jaccard, phoneme Levenshtein, and character TF-IDF. We reveal that while average pooling almost entirely fails to capture character-level edit distances, path signatures strongly align with them, with depth 2 signatures optimally balancing character and word-level sensitivities. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the critical lexical variance is concentrated in a highly compact PCA subspace, and unlike pooling, signatures structurally preserve and quantify word order. These findings establish path signatures not as semantic generalizers, but as rigorous mathematical lenses that explicitly encode discrete lexical structures and word order, offering an interpretable alternative to opaque deep learning for lexical tracking.

papers.title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
papers.summary: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation. While faithful to the underlying XAI methods, these pipelines are hard to adapt and often struggle with context-dependent follow-up questions. We present SimXAI, a lightweight LLM-centric conversational layer that replaces these modules with a single tool-calling LLM that bridges access to existing XAI resources. Rather than a standalone agent, SimXAI serves as a modular interface that enables conversational access to external XAI resources. We further introduce an evaluation suite for single- and multi-turn parsing, faithfulness, and contextualization. Across existing and new datasets, SimXAI achieves strong function-selection accuracy and high faithfulness while better handling context-dependent requests. In a user study replacing only the conversational layer of TalkToModel, a representative GUS-based agent, users completed tasks more accurately and in fewer turn. Overall, SimXAI improves GUS-based design while preserving faithfulness and improving conversational quality.

papers.title: Text as an Index for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Knowledge Tracing
papers.summary: Knowledge tracing (KT) predicts a student's next response from their history. New platforms often have question texts but no response logs for training, motivating zero-shot cross-domain KT. Existing transfer and cold-start methods use question semantics, but cross-platform semantic discrepancies limit transferability. We propose TIZSKT, which separates behavioral sequence modeling from domain-local historical evidence construction and uses text as an index rather than a directly transferable predictive representation. The Mastery-Dynamics Encoder learns correctness dynamics without question identifiers or text embeddings. Domain-Local Question Addressing builds fixed question addresses using a frozen text encoder and an unsupervised per-domain projection. The Text-Addressing Kernel uses these addresses to aggregate the current student's previous outcomes into a question-specific historical correctness summary.
